# Laravel and Symfony security

- Use Form Requests/Symfony validation and explicit DTO/entity mapping. Keep `$fillable` narrow, never set `$guarded = []`, and do not use `forceFill`/request-all on privileged models.
- Use Eloquent/Doctrine parameter binding. For unavoidable raw clauses, bind every value and map identifiers/sort fields to an allowlist.
- Preserve Blade `{{ }}` and Twig autoescaping. Avoid `{!! !!}`, `|raw`, and dynamically generated template names/source for untrusted content.
- Apply Policies/Gates/Symfony voters to the loaded resource and action for every controller, API route, queued job, download, and alternate write path.
- Scope route-model binding/repository queries to the authenticated tenant/owner or authorize immediately after load. An opaque route key does not prevent IDOR.
- Keep CSRF enabled for cookie-authenticated routes and separate truly stateless token APIs. Configure secure session cookies and rotate sessions after login.
- Keep `APP_KEY`, `APP_SECRET`, credentials, and `.env` external and inaccessible from the web root. Disable debug/profiler outside trusted development.
- Validate queued job/event class and payload types; do not deserialize arbitrary client-controlled PHP objects or dispatch a user-selected class.
- Generate upload names, validate actual content, store outside executable paths, and authorize temporary/signed URLs at creation and use.
- Use framework rate limiters for authentication/recovery and costly routes, with account plus trusted source context and consistent failure responses.
